title: Dimension of fibres in a fibre-component closure inside a flat family
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a flat morphism [def-weil-flat-morphism] of schemes, locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $t,s\in S$, and let $y$ be the generic point [def-sc-generic-point] of an irreducible component $B$ [def-weil-irreducible-components] of the scheme-theoretic fibre $X_t$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Regard $y$ as a point of $X$ via the fibre inclusion. Give $Z=\overline{\{y\}}\subseteq |X|$ and $Z_s=Z\cap f^{-1}(s)$ their subspace topologies. For every irreducible component $D$ of $Z_s$, its topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] equals that of $B$: $\dim D=\dim B$. No flatness of the reduced closed subscheme with underlying space $Z$, no integrality of $S$, and no purity assumption on the other components of $X_t$ are required.

source.place: Tag 0GSJ (lemma-flat-associated-equidimensional), part (2), specialized to F=O_X and a fibre-component generic point; pointwise input Tag 0GSI (lemma-associated-point-specializes). The reduced closure Y of y has Y_t with underlying space B; relative dimension is defined by Morphisms Tag 02NJ.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_X$. Because $f$ is flat, $\mathcal F$ is flat over $S$ at every point. The generic point of an irreducible component $B$ of the locally Noetherian fibre $X_t$ is an associated point of the fibre structure sheaf, hence belongs to the relative assassin $\operatorname{Ass}_{X/S}(\mathcal O_X)$ by the fibrewise definition of the relative assassin.

source.place: Tag 05AT (definition-relative-assassin) and Tag 05AH (lemma-minimal-support-in-ass), applied to the structure sheaf of the fibre X_t

proof.text: Apply the flat-associated-equidimensional lemma to $f$, $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_X$, and the relative associated point $y$. Its closure $Y$ is the reduced integral closed subscheme with underlying space $Z=\overline{\{y\}}$, and $T$ is the closure of $\{f(y)\}$. The flatness hypothesis at generic points of fibres of $Y\to T$ holds because $f$ is flat everywhere. The lemma gives an integer $d$ such that $Y\to T$ has relative dimension $d$, and every generic point of every irreducible component of a fibre $Y_s$ has local dimension $d$.

The fibre $Y_t$ has underlying topological space $B$: it is the closure of the generic point $y$ inside the fibre $X_t$, and $B$ is the irreducible component whose generic point is $y$. Thus $d=\dim B$. For any $s\in S$, the subspace $Y_s$ has the same underlying space as $Z_s$, and its irreducible components are exactly the $D$ in the statement. The relative-dimension conclusion therefore gives $\dim D=d=\dim B$ for every irreducible component $D$ of $Z_s$. No reducedness or flatness of $Y$ is used; only the flatness of $\mathcal O_X$ over $S$ enters the cited lemma.

lean.statement: theorem flat_fibre_component_closure_dimension {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [Flat f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (t s : S) (B : Set (f.fiber t)) (hB : B ∈ irreducibleComponents (f.fiber t)) (y : f.fiber t) (hy : IsGenericPoint y B) : ∀ (D : Set (Set.inter (closure ({f.fiberι t y} : Set X)) ((f.base : X → S) ⁻¹' ({s} : Set S)))), D ∈ irreducibleComponents (Set.inter (closure ({f.fiberι t y} : Set X)) ((f.base : X → S) ⁻¹' ({s} : Set S))) → topologicalKrullDim D = topologicalKrullDim B
